title: ÆTHER: Friday Night (electro nu-disco, funky bassline)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: A brand-new electro disco / nu-disco track built around a FUNKY BASSLINE, ONE continuous piece on ONE hook from the first second to the last. Exactly 120 BPM, A Dorian (A B C D E F-sharp G), straight four-on-the-floor disco groove with a human, swinging sixteenth feel. The bassline is the star, written out: a fat electric bass playing A with an octave slap pop on the off-beat, ghost-note sixteenths, a walk-up C, D, E into G, then a slide down from E to A; it keeps moving like a second melody all the way through. The hook, written out: A, A, C, D, slide up to E, lean on F-sharp with a shake, E, D, C, D; the answer: G, F-sharp, E, D, C, B, A. Sung-style phrasing with slides and bends on whatever plays it. Every section uses THIS SAME hook, varied and growing, never a new tune. Instruments: electric bass (slap and finger), real disco drum kit with open hi-hats and hand claps, chicken-scratch funk guitar, wah guitar, clavinet, Rhodes electric piano, a bright analog synth lead, warm analog pads, a disco string section, a disco horn section, and a soft wordless female voice humming 'ooh' (no words, no shouted chants). Real instruments sound close and natural, no heavy echo. 0-4 s: the funky bassline ALONE, dry and fat, a slap octave pop on beat one. 4-8 s: kick on every beat and off-beat open hi-hat join. 8-16 s: chicken-scratch guitar, clavinet, claps on 2 and 4, warm pad. 16-28 s: the hook on the bright synth lead, disco string stabs answer it. 28-38 s: the soft female voice hums the hook back, Rhodes chords underneath. 38-48 s: the violins play a fast up-run with slides, then strings and synth lead play the hook together, bigger. 48-56 s: the drums step out to just hi-hats and claps while the bass plays a funky slap-bass solo break; the last bar is only the female voice holding a long note. 56-72 s: the full band slams back in, the hook on the disco horn section with a string counter-melody, then the wah guitar and synth lead trade the hook back and forth, faster each time. 72-84 s: final chorus, the biggest moment: the bassline doubles into sixteenths, voice and strings in unison on the hook, horns punching the accents. 84-90 s: the whole band plays the hook's last phrase as tight unison stabs, then a full stop. 90-96 s: the bass alone plays the opening line once more and ends on a slap octave A, one string run up, the last note rings. Glossy, wide, punchy modern nu-disco mix with deep sub bass and the bass clearly upfront. Not EDM, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no filter sweeps, no build-and-drop, no fade-out. Do not use a rising three-note root-third-fifth call, shouted 'hey' chants, reversed swells, thavil or nadaswaram anywhere.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 17:41: 'New disco track - genre - electro disco Nu-Disco, Funky Bassline'. Modern theme (no kings). Script first (rule 17), raga Kharaharapriya in A = Dorian, the funk mode (rule 19). Kept fresh after the Storm Entry repetition note: its own written hook and bassline, none of the shared devices (3-note call, hey chants, reversed swell, thavil/nadaswaram mass BGM).

story: Friday midnight in Bengaluru: a developer shuts her laptop after a brutal release week, rides the empty metro and dances with her friends on a rooftop until sunrise.
